Zero algorithmic time, many initial conditions
----------------------------------------------
We first test the "zero step" (extending maximum and minimum conditioned evolutions
using an essentially empty innovation) over a range of initial conditions.
In this edge-case it is necessary to build the constructed `CEvolution` from the
null `Innovation` `iv` in order to ensure all fields are filled as required!
Note the fudge to make sure that the `CRemoval` list is unchanged. Note too
the monotonicity test using `ev_pair`.
```{julia simulation1}
iv = Innovation(population, I[], R[], 
    C[C(t,population) for (r, t) ∈ enumerate(cremoval_times)])
crcount = length(cremoval_times)
traj_hi = [P(0, r, r+1) for r ∈ 1:population] ∪ iv.cremovals
traj_lo = sort([P(t, r, r+1) for (r,t) ∈ enumerate(cremoval_times)][1:end-1] 
    ∪ [C(t, r) for (r,t) ∈ enumerate(cremoval_times)])

for i ∈ 1:population
    initial = SIR(0, population - i, i, 0)
    startup = initial.i + initial.r
    ev_hi  = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, cremoval_times)
    ev_lo  = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, cremoval_times; maximal=false)
    ev_pair = []
    for (ev, traj, kind) ∈ [(ev_hi, traj_hi, "HI"), (ev_lo, traj_lo, "LO")]
        @debug "Step $i $kind"
        computed_LFE = convert(Vector{AI}, [z for z ∈ traj if
                ! (z isa OperativeInfection) || startup < z.infectee ≤ crcount])
        LFE = last_feasible_evolution(duration, ev, iv)
        @test CEvolution(ev.initial, LFE).history == LFE
        @test computed_LFE == sort(ev.cremovals ∪ ev.removals ∪ 
            [P(z) for z ∈ ev.infections if
                z isa OperativeInfection && startup < z.infectee ≤ crcount])
         
        evx = ev ∘ iv # Need to restore `cremovals` of `ev` (resp. `ev_hi` or `ev_lo`)
        # FUDGE STARTS
        deleteat!(evx.cremovals, 1:length(ev.cremovals))
        append!(evx.cremovals, ev.cremovals)
        # FUDGE ENDS

        @test ev.removals == evx.removals
        @test ev.cremovals == evx.cremovals
        @test ev.trajectory == evx.trajectory
        @test EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(evx)
        push!(ev_pair, evx)
    end
    @test ev_pair[1] ⪯ ev_pair[2]
end ;
```
These `@test`s check respectively

 * that the `LFE` reconstructed from the resulting `CEvolution` 
(a rather trivial calculation in these edge-cases) agrees with the `LFE` computed using `last_feasible_evolution`;
 * that the \LFE will be the history (hence _a fortiori_ the `LFE`) of of an epidemic
generated using this `LFE` (This check should hold in all cases, not just the above edge-cases);
 * that the \LFE is genuinely the least feasible evolution;
 * and that the constructed "`HI`" and "`LO`" `CEvolutions` are in weakly monotonic relationship.

These `@test`s check respectively

 * that the \LFE computed using `last_feasible_evolution` agrees with what is stored in the `CEvolution` field;
 * that this \LFE is the history (hence _a fortiori_ the `LFE`) of an epidemic generated using the self-same `LFE`;
 * that the \LFE is genuinely the least feasible evolution;
 * and that the constructed "`HI`" and "`LO`" `CEvolutions` are in weakly monotonic relationship.

Also an attempt to check coalescence is permanent: not currently working!

\appendix
# Appendices {.unnumbered}

Towards a correct and robust generation of `LFE`
================================================
We have introduced a new function to construct the `LFE`.
Note that it does not assume `ev.infections` to have 
been categorized as `OperativeInfection` versus `InoperativeInfection`.
Here is a (non-executable) listing, listed for purposes of debugging.
```julia
function last_feasible_evolution(duration::Real, 
    # last_feasible_evolution = EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution
    # resulting_cremovals     = EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals
    ev::AbstractEvolution, iv::Innovation) ::Vector{AbstractIncident}
    
    recomputed_cremovals = resulting_cremovals(ev, iv) 
    previous_infections  = [PInfection(z) for z ∈ ev.chronology if z isa OperativeInfection]
    chronology = sort(iv.infections ∪ previous_infections ∪ recomputed_cremovals)
    
    removal_boundary =
        accumulate(+, z isa CRemoval ? 1 : 0 for z ∈ chronology, init=ev.initial.r)
    @assert any(z isa KilledInfection ? z.target ≤ rb : z.target > rb for 
                                    (z, rb) ∈ zip(ev.chronology, removal_boundary))  
    
    raw_chronology = [z isa OperativeInfection && z.target ≤ rb ? KilledInfection(z) : z
            for (z, rb) ∈ zip(chronology, removal_boundary)]
    relevant_chronology = filter(z -> !(z isa KilledInfection), raw_chronology)
    
    removal_fence =
        accumulate(max, z isa CRemoval ? z.target : 1 for z ∈ relevant_chronology)
    
    current_timeline = removal_fence[end]
    reverse_LFE = AbstractIncident[]
    for (z, rf) ∈ Base.Iterators.reverse(zip(relevant_chronology, removal_fence))
        if z isa CRemoval
            push!(reverse_LFE, z)
        elseif z isa OperativeInfection && 
                current_timeline > max(ev.initial.i, rf) &&
                z.infectee == current_timeline 
            push!(reverse_LFE, z)
            current_timeline -= 1
        end
    end
    
    return reverse(reverse_LFE)
end
```


Checking `LFE`
==============
The following produces a useful test of `LFE`
 (non-executable listing, listed for purposes of debugging).
```julia
# import EpidemicsCFTP: evolution, evolution_history, NonMinimalLFE, EmptyLFE
function is_correct_LFE(ev::CEvolution; debug::Bool=false)::Bool
    if isempty(ev.LFE)
        throw(EmptyLFE(ev))
    end

    cycle = evolution(ev.initial, ev.LFE)[1]
    (state, pointer) = iterate(cycle)
    @debug println("state:     ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev.history)) 
    @debug println("state:     ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev.LFE)) 
    @debug println("state:     ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), sort(ev.history ∪ ev.LFE)))
    for z ∈ sort(ev.history ∪ ev.LFE)
        if z ∈ ev.LFE
            @debug println("state:     ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), (z, state)))
        end
        if z ∈ ev.LFE && z isa OperativeInfection
            chron0 = filter(!=(z), ev.chronology)
            try
                state_plus = SIR(z.t, state.s, state.i, state.r)
                violation = evolution_history(state_plus, chron0; conditioned=true)
                @debug println("state:     ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), state))
                @debug println("chron0:    ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), chron0))
                @debug println("deleted:   ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), z))
                @debug println("full path: ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), violation))
            catch e
                @debug e
            else
                @debug println("$pointer: ", sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), z))
                throw(NonMinimalLFE(ev))
            end
        end
        if z ∈ ev.LFE
            (state, pointer) = iterate(cycle, pointer)
        end
    end
    return true
end
```

The `one_stop` function
=======================
The `one_step` function corresponds to the method `CEvolution(::AbstractEvolution, ::Innovation)`,
listed for purposes of debugging.
```julia
# Actually a method of `EpidemicsCFTP.CEvolution`: see also `∘` in next section!
# import EpidemicsCFTP: inactive_removals, resulting_cremovals, last_feasible_evolution
function CEvolution(ev::AbstractEvolution, iv::Innovation)::CEvolution
    # inactive_removals = EpidemicsCFTP.inactive_removals
    # resulting_cremovals = EpidemicsCFTP.resulting_cremovals
    # last_feasible_evolution = EpidemicsCFTP.last_feasible_evolution
    # Step 1.
    @assert length(ev.cremovals) == length(iv.cremovals)
    @assert all(x.t == y.t for (x,y) ∈ zip(ev.cremovals, iv.cremovals))
    
    # Step 2.
    removals = inactive_removals(ev, iv)
    
    # Step 3.
    recomputed_cremovals  = resulting_cremovals(ev, iv.cremovals)
    
    # Step 4.
    duration = maximum(z.t for z ∈ recomputed_cremovals)
    LFE = last_feasible_evolution(duration, ev, iv)
    perpetuated_infections = [z for z ∈ LFE if z isa PInfection] 
    
    # Step 5.
    # * Initial computation of `NFZ2`, a **list of times** 
    # indexed by time line ("level"), where each time is initially defined as
    # the supremum of times of **inactivated** `Removal`s at given level or 
    # below. So the envelope increases monotonically with level.
    NFZ1 = repeat([-Inf], ev.initial.n)
    for z ∈ [z for z ∈ removals if z < ev.finis[z.target]]
        NFZ1[z.target] = max(NFZ1[z.target], z.t)
    end
    NFZ2 = accumulate(max, NFZ1)
 
    # The hard work begins! We generate the NFZ3.
    # * The list `processed_infections` of processed `AbstractInfection`s will
    # eventually store (initially in reverse time order) an adjusted version of
    # each infection supplied by the new `Innovation` `iv`.
	processed_infections = AbstractInfection[]
	NFZ3 = deepcopy(NFZ2)
	
	# * Iteration: work backwards through `Infection`s supplied by `iv`
	# together with perpetuated infections,
    # determining in each case how to transform the supplied `Infection`
    # when adding it to the list `processed_infections`.
	for z ∈ reverse(sort(iv.infections ∪ perpetuated_infections))
	    
	    # * If the `Infection` `z` has `target` on the removed portion of a level
        # then it will never be activated, so add `z` as a `KilledInfection`.
	    if (z ≥ ev.finis[z.target])
	        push!(processed_infections, KilledInfection(z))
	        continue
	    end
	    
	    # * If the `Infection` `z` potentially infects a level at a _later time_ 
        # than the current `NFZ2` at that level, then its activation will
        # never break the conditioning (**needs proof!**), so add `z` as-is.
        # (I think the point is: since we are working backwards in time, once
        # `z.t` is considered then `NFZ2` is frozen from time `t` onwards.)
	    #
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z < ev.finis[z.target])
	    #
        if (z.t ≥ NFZ3[z.infectee])
	        push!(processed_infections, z)
	        continue
	    end
	    
	    # * However if `z.t < NFZ2[z.infectee - 1]` then no issue can arise, as 
        # infection of the level immediately below `z.infectee` will then not be
        # allowed at this time. So again add `z` as-is.
        #
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z < ev.finis[z.target])
	    @assert(z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee])
	    #
        if (z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee - 1])
	        push!(processed_infections, z)
	        continue
	    end
	    
	    # * Suppose `z ≥ ev.start[z.target]`: then an issue would arise
        # if the level at `z.infectee - 1` were to become infected before `z.t`. 
        #
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee])
	    @assert(z.t ≥ NFZ3[z.infectee - 1])
	    @assert(z < ev.finis[z.target])
	    #
	    # One of two cases must hold:
	    #
	    # * Case (a): Suppose `z < ev.start[z.infectee - 1]`.
        # Then **increase** `NFZ2[z.infectee - 1]` to `z.t` in order to
        # preclude the time line getting infected, and also transform `z` to a
        # `NoFlyInfection` when added to `processed_infections`, to signal
        # that it should never become infected.  
        # Case (b): Alternatively, suppose `z ≥ ev.start[z.infectee - 1]`.
        # Then increasing `NFZ2[z.infectee - 1]` to `z.t` would lead to a
        # problem, since this level is infected at time `z.t`. Therefore we
        # transform `z` to a `ExpungedInfection` when we add it to 
        # `processed_infections`, so that it is treated as an
        # `InoperativeInfection`.
	    if (z ≥ ev.start[z.target])
            if (z < ev.start[z.infectee - 1])
                NFZ3[z.infectee - 1] = z.t
                push!(processed_infections, NoFlyInfection(z))
                # Uncomment for tracking information
                # @info "Conversion of infection into $(NoFlyInfection(z))"
                continue
            else 
                push!(processed_infections, ExpungedInfection(z))
                # Uncomment for tracking information
                # @info "Conversion of infection into $(ExpungedInfection(z))"
                continue 
            end 
	    end
	    
	    # At this stage of the iteration 
	    @assert(z.t < NFZ3[z.infectee])
	    @assert(z.t ≥ NFZ3[z.infectee - 1])
	    @assert(z < ev.start[z.target])
	    # 
	    # * Consider now that potential `Infection`s to be treated later in this
        # iteration must have time mark earlier than `z.t`. If one of these were
        # to infect the level `z.infectee - 1` then it would follow by monotonicity
        # that the `z.target` level would become infected by that time `z.t`; and 
        # thus would create an infection of the `z.infectee` level at time `z.t`. 
        # In order for this to be prevented, we need to extend the `NFZ2` 
        # at level `z.infectee - 1` up to time `z.t`. We also transform `z`
        # to a `NoFlyInfection` when we add it to `processed_infections`, to
        # signal that it should never become infected.
	    NFZ3[z.infectee - 1] = z.t 
	    push!(processed_infections, NoFlyInfection(z))
        # Uncomment for tracking information
        # @info "Conversion of infection into $(NoFlyInfection(z))"
	
	end
    
    # Return the new `CEvolution`: NOTE it is built using a new `Innovation` `iv_mod`!
    iv_mod = Innovation(ev.initial.n, processed_infections, removals, recomputed_cremovals)
    return CEvolution(ev.initial, iv_mod, LFE=LFE, NFZ1=NFZ1, NFZ2=NFZ2, NFZ3=NFZ3)
end
```

Notation
========
We need to be able to (weakly) compare two `AbstractEvolution`s,
using `⪯` (`\preceq`).
```julia
import EpidemicsCFTP: AbstractEvolution, CEvolution
import EpidemicsCFTP: AbstractEvolution
function ⪯(ev1::AbstractEvolution, ev2::AbstractEvolution) ::Bool
    ev1.initial.n == ev2.initial.n || return false
    return all(z1 ≤ z2 for (z1, z2) ∈ zip(ev1.start, ev2.start))
end ;

function ⪯(ev1::CEvolution, ev2::CEvolution) ::Bool
    any(ev1.initial.n != ev2.initial.n) && error("populations differ")
    pair = zip(ev1.cremovals, ev2.cremovals)
    any(z1.t != z2.t  for (z1, z2) ∈ pair) && error("cremoval times differ")
    timelines_ok = all(z1 ≤ z2 for (z1, z2) ∈ zip(ev1.start, ev2.start))
    crtargets_ok = all(z1.target ≥ z2.target for (z1, z2) ∈ pair)
    return timelines_ok && crtargets_ok 
end ;

weq = ⪯
```


It is also useful to be able to compose a `CEvolution` with an `Innovation`
(non-commutative!) using `∘` (`\circ`).
```julia
import EpidemicsCFTP: CEvolution, Innovation
function ∘(cev::CEvolution, iv::Innovation) ::CEvolution
    return CEvolution(cev, iv)
end ;
```
